content:
**Top 5 best‑selling video games (worldwide, all platforms)**  

| Rank | Game | Approx. units sold* | Primary genre(s) |
|------|------|--------------------|------------------|
| 1 | **Minecraft** | ≈ 300 million | Sandbox / Survival / Open‑world building |
| 2 | **Grand Theft Auto V** | ≈ 190 million | Action‑adventure / Open‑world crime drama |
| 3 | **Tetris** (EA Mobile version) | ≈ 100 million | Puzzle (falling‑block) |
| 4 | **Wii Sports** | ≈ 82.9 million | Sports (simulation of multiple Olympic‑style events) |
| 5 | **PUBG: Battlegrounds** | ≈ 75 million | Battle‑royale / Online multiplayer shooter |

\*Sales figures are the most recent worldwide totals reported on the Wikipedia “List of best‑selling video games” page (as of 2023‑2024). They include all platforms on which each title has been released.

**Brief genre notes**

- **Minecraft** – A sandbox game that lets players freely explore, gather resources, craft items, and build virtually anything. Its survival mode adds combat and health management, but the core experience is open‑world creation.  
- **Grand Theft Auto V** – An open‑world action‑adventure game set in a modern city. It mixes driving, shooting, story missions, and a persistent online component (GTA Online).  
- **Tetris** – A timeless puzzle game where players rotate and stack falling tetrominoes to clear lines. The EA Mobile version is the most‑sold incarnation of the classic title.  
- **Wii Sports** – A collection of motion‑controlled sports mini‑games (tennis, bowling, baseball, golf, boxing). It serves as a casual, family‑friendly sports simulation.  
- **PUBG: Battlegrounds** – A multiplayer online battle‑royale shooter where up to 100 players parachute onto an island, scavenge gear, and fight to be the last survivor.  

These five titles together account for well over **700 million** copies sold, making them the highest‑selling video games in history to date.
